encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a flow_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_profile is minimal_encrypted or stronger.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a ContentBlock for Flow synthesis content.

state.description: Flow lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: cx.flow.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=flow_not_active); cx.flow.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else flow_not_archived); terminal state is reached only via a cx.redaction event targeting the flow (MUST come from {'active','archived'} else flow_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding cx.flow.archive / cx.flow.restore / cx.redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

stage.description: Flow business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle): archive does NOT change stage; stage=done does NOT auto-archive. Required on cx.flow.create (no protocol-level default). The only wire path that mutates stage is the dedicated cx.flow.stage.set event; cx.flow.update patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected (schema_violation, single-source). Stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note field — the cx.flow.stage.set event log is the audit source, and human-readable explanations belong in a Message on the discussion track that references the event. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond the core reducer hard invariants (terminal state freeze, non-active reject) defined in models/common-fields.md §5.3.3. See models/flow-and-message.md §3.2 for full semantics and models/common-fields.md §5.3 for the protocol-level enum / bucket mapping.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering cx.flow.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions (stage value unchanged) MUST NOT update this field.

tracks.description: Active Flow tracks, keyed by track name. Tracks are pure section pointers (synthesis vs discussion timeline) — they do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. The entire Flow shares a single effective scope determined by Flow.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md); there is no per-track security boundary. At most one track entry may explicitly set is_primary=true; when none does, the reducer derives the primary track by the deterministic rules in models/flow-and-message.md §4.5. The map MUST contain at least one entry; track names are validated by propertyNames.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle (see models/circle.md) that defines this Flow's effective scope. When set, ALL Flow tracks (synthesis, discussion, etc.) share that Circle's membership, history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and encryption_profile. When unset, the Flow lives in Realm-default scope. The referenced Circle MUST have realm_id == this Flow's realm_id (reducer enforces; otherwise schema_violation reason=circle_realm_mismatch). Reducer stamps the immutable effective_scope onto each emitted Event; rebinding scope_circle_id is forbidden by default (failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden). For 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion' scenarios use two Flows linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation (circle.md §7.2).

not.$comment: Reject legacy discriminator `type`, legacy composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`; canonical content blocks use `kind`, composite children use `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes`.

flow_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Flow metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Flow metadata fields. Reducer-owned fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

flow_track.description: Flow track entry — a pure section pointer (synthesis vs discussion timeline). The track's stable name is the map key in Flow.tracks; this object holds the track's per-entry config. Tracks do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. The whole Flow has a single effective scope determined by Flow.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md); there is no per-track security boundary. To represent 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion', create two Flows linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation per models/circle.md §7.2.

enabled.description: Whether this track currently accepts new writes (synthesis edits / discussion messages). Default true when omitted. Setting enabled=false MUST cause the reducer to reject subsequent writes to this track with 'track_disabled' until enabled is set back to true. Disabling a track does NOT delete prior history; it freezes new writes only. UI MAY hide a disabled track or render it read-only.

metadata.description: Track-local UI metadata. It does not create membership, history visibility, or E2EE scope.

not.$comment: Legacy track-local extension field; canonical name is metadata.
